back: A named, versioned pointer to data, so a job refers to a name and version rather than a path someone may move. Keyword: versioned pointer.
A versioned definition of the software a job runs in. Pinning it is what makes a run reproducible later. Keyword: reproducibility.
Shares assets across workspaces — train in dev, register once, deploy to test and prod from there. Keyword: promote, don't retrain.
Instance is one personal dev machine. Cluster scales out for training and back to zero when idle. Keyword: clusters for training.
Credential stores a key or SAS. Identity-based uses Entra, so access is auditable and revocable per person. Keyword: prefer identity.
Can run jobs and register models but cannot create compute — which keeps cost control with the platform team. Keyword: no compute creation.
Private endpoints to storage, Key Vault, and Container Registry, with explicit outbound rules. Keyword: isolate the workspace.
A federated credential — the workflow exchanges its own token, so no secret sits in the repository. Keyword: no repo secret.
Scripts, pipelines, environment specs, IaC, prompts. Not data or model binaries — those are versioned assets. Keyword: code yes, blobs no.
Captures parameters, metrics, and artifacts for common frameworks without instrumenting the script. Keyword: tracking for free.
Grid for small discrete spaces, random for breadth, Bayesian for efficiency when runs are expensive. Keyword: match to cost.
Bandit or median stopping kills unpromising trials so compute is not spent on them. Keyword: stop the losers.
The fast route to a baseline across algorithms and preprocessing — not a replacement for judgement. Keyword: baseline.
It carries the signature and environment, so deployment needs no hand-written scoring script. Keyword: no scoring script.
Packaged with the model so inference reproduces training exactly. The defence against training-serving skew. Keyword: same features.
Error analysis, interpretability, fairness across cohorts, counterfactuals, causal inference — used before promotion. Keyword: aggregate accuracy hides cohorts.
Online serves real-time over HTTPS and is provisioned continuously. Batch scores large volumes asynchronously. Keyword: don't pay for idle.
New deployment alongside the old, a small traffic share, metrics watched, share increased only if they hold. Keyword: shift gradually.
Set the traffic split back to zero — immediate, no redeployment. Keyword: instant reversal.
Copies live requests to a candidate without returning its responses, exercising it on real traffic at no risk. Keyword: shadow.
Data drift is the inputs changing. Concept drift is the input-to-target relationship changing, inputs unchanged. Keyword: inputs vs relationship.
It usually cannot be confirmed until ground-truth labels arrive, so a monitoring design must say where labels come from. Keyword: needs labels.

front: What a drift alert should do
back: Trigger a defined response — retrain, investigate, or roll back — not an email nobody owns. Keyword: alerts need owners.
Holds the details of a dependency such as a search index, and can authenticate with a managed identity rather than a key. Keyword: keyless dependency.
Who may create and change deployments versus who may only call them — deployment rights are cost rights. Keyword: deploy equals spend.
Serverless bills per token with no capacity planning. Managed compute is dedicated infrastructure you size and pay for regardless. Keyword: shared vs dedicated.
Reserved capacity giving predictable latency and no throttling at fixed cost. The answer to 'must not be rate limited'. Keyword: reserved.
A production deployment names a version rather than following latest — a silent upgrade changes behaviour under an evaluated system. Keyword: don't float.
Reviewed as a diff, released with a version, revertible. Editing in a portal makes a regression untraceable. Keyword: prompt is code.
Evaluate against a dataset, compare with the baseline, promote the winner. Not intuition. Keyword: measured promotion.
A tokens-per-minute limit stops a runaway agent loop consuming a month's budget in an afternoon. Keyword: blast radius on cost.
Monitor token consumption per feature; without attribution a cost problem cannot be targeted. Keyword: per feature.
Bicep and the Azure CLI, so test and production are identical rather than configured twice by hand. Keyword: declare it.
Same shape as MLOps — candidate alongside, shift traffic gradually, keep the ability to move back. Keyword: same discipline.
Smaller model for narrow, high-volume tasks; a reasoning model only for genuinely multi-step problems. Keyword: don't overspend on thinking.
Tells the evaluator which column is question, response, context, and ground truth. A mapping error yields plausible meaningless scores. Keyword: check it first.
Is the answer supported by the retrieved context? Needs context, not ground truth. Keyword: supported by source.
Similarity and F1 do. Groundedness, relevance, coherence, and fluency do not. Keyword: only comparison metrics.
The evaluator says how often the system would fail; the filter stops one failure reaching a user. You need both. Keyword: measure vs block.
Catch organisation-specific rules — a phrase that must appear, a claim never to be made — that generic metrics miss. Keyword: your rules.
Samples production traffic and runs evaluators against it, catching decay a pre-release run cannot. Keyword: after release.
Rising prompt tokens means context or history growing; rising completion tokens means too much output. Keyword: split the bill.
A retrieval miss, a bad tool choice, and a prompt fault look identical from outside. Keyword: attribute the failure.
Retrieval quality caps the answer, so establish whether the right passage was found before touching the prompt. Keyword: diagnose in order.

front: Similarity threshold too high or low
back: Too high returns nothing for legitimate questions; too low pads the prompt with noise the model must ignore. Keyword: both directions hurt.
Invalidates existing vectors — the whole index must be re-embedded. Plan it, don't discover it. Keyword: full re-index.
Offline is cheap and safe and comes first; A/B settles how real users behave. Keyword: both, in that order.
LoRA trains a small set of additional parameters and is far cheaper to train and host. Keyword: parameter-efficient.
A few hundred consistent, well-formed examples beat thousands of noisy ones. Keyword: quality over quantity.
It propagates the generating model's own biases and errors into the fine-tuned model. Keyword: review it.
